template.name: Patient Monitor and OR Modules
template.desc: Class I, CF applied parts (SpO2, ECG, Temp). Converted from the Ansur template.

steps.title: Visual inspection
steps.instructions: Inspect the monitor, modules, cables and accessories.

items: The case, display screen, buttons, power cord, and accessories have no obvious signs of damage.
The external connecting cables are not frayed and the connector pins are not loose or bent.
The external connectors are not loose and their pins are not bent.
The safety labels and data plate are clearly legible.
The power-on test is passed. The power indicator and alarm system works correctly and the monitor starts up properly.

steps.title: Mains voltage
steps.instructions:
Set up for the electrical safety tests:
1. Plug the ESA612 into the mains supply.
2. Connect the monitor’s power cord to the ESA612 equipment outlet and make sure the monitor is switched on.
3. Connect the applied parts (SpO2, ECG, Temp) to the monitor and their leads to the ESA612 applied-part posts.
4. Check the applied parts on the patient leakage step match what is connected (Change applied parts to add a group or change its type).
Then start the auto sequence: it runs all the electrical safety tests and only pauses to move the test lead.

steps.title: Protective earth resistance
steps.instructions: Connect the device’s mains lead to the ESA612 equipment outlet. Clip the red test lead to an exposed earthed metal part, such as a rear-panel screw.

steps.title: Insulation: mains to protective earth
steps.instructions: Connect the device’s mains lead to the ESA612 equipment outlet and switch the device on. Don’t touch the device during the test.

steps.title: Insulation: applied parts to protective earth
steps.instructions: Recorded only. The Ansur template sets no limit for this measurement.

steps.title: Enclosure leakage
steps.instructions:
Connect the test lead to a conductive non-earthed exposed part on the monitor.
Note: only a representative sample of conductive non-earthed exposed parts needs to be tested.

steps.title: Earth leakage
steps.instructions: Connect the device’s mains lead to the ESA612 equipment outlet. The device will be switched on and off between conditions. Limits: 5000 µA normal, 10000 µA neutral open (AS/NZS 3551:2012+A2 B11.6).

steps.title: Patient leakage
steps.instructions: Connect each applied part (patient cable, sensor) to its ESA612 posts. Connect the device’s mains lead to the ESA612 equipment outlet.

steps.title: Mains on applied parts
steps.instructions: Connect each applied part (patient cable, sensor) to its ESA612 posts. Connect the device’s mains lead to the ESA612 equipment outlet.

steps.title: ECG: heart rate, waveform and lead off
steps.instructions:
Connect the ECG leads to the ProSim 8. The simulator is set to ECG sinus rhythm, 60 bpm, 1 mV.
1. Enter the HR shown on the monitor (60±1 bpm).
2. Check the ECG waves are displayed correctly without noise.
3. Disconnect each lead in turn and check the matching lead off message appears. Reconnect all leads.

extra.label: ECG waves are displayed correctly without noise.
ECG Lead Off alarm appears correctly for each lead.

steps.title: ECG: calibration square wave
steps.instructions: The simulator outputs a square wave (performance). Set the ECG filter on the monitor to Diagnostic and verify the wave scale difference does not exceed 5%.

monitor.label: The difference between the amplitude of the ECG calibration square wave and that of the wave scale is not greater than 5%.

steps.title: ECG: paced signals
steps.instructions: The simulator outputs a paced signal. Set Paced to Yes on the monitor and check the pace pulse marks on the screen.

monitor.label: Paced signals are detected and pace pulse marks are displayed when [Paced] is set to [Yes].

steps.title: Respiration
steps.instructions: The simulator outputs respiration at 20 rpm. Verify the Resp wave is not distorted and enter the Resp rate shown on the monitor (20±2).

extra.label: The Resp wave is not distorted.

steps.title: Temperature
steps.instructions: The simulator outputs 37.0 °C. Check every temperature channel on the monitor.

monitor.label: The value displayed for each Temp channel of the monitor is within 37±0.1 °C

steps.title: IBP: static pressure, both channels
steps.instructions: Zero the IBP on the monitor first. The simulator sets channels 1 and 2 to 200 mmHg. Enter what the monitor shows (196–204 mmHg). Mark channel 2 N/A if the monitor has only one IBP channel.

steps.title: IBP: ART and LV waveforms
steps.instructions: The simulator outputs ART on channel 1 and LV on channel 2. Swap the channels with a second run if needed, so each channel is checked with both waves.

monitor.label: The ART and LV waves for each IBP channel are displayed correctly.

steps.title: SpO2 and NIBP
steps.instructions:
SpO2: measure SpO2 on a healthy person’s finger. Check a Pleth wave and PR value are displayed, then enter the displayed SpO2 (95–100%).

NIBP accuracy and leakage: 1. Set Patient Category to Adult.
2. Connect the NIBP cuff to the NIBP connector on the monitor.
3. Wrap the cuff around the cylinder.
4. Select Main Menu → System → Maintenance → Module → NIBP → NIBP Leakage Test. The message "Leakage Testing…" is displayed in the NIBP parameter area.
5. Verify the difference between the simulator and monitor is within 3mmHg/min. After about 20s, the cuff automatically deflates, which indicates that the NIBP leakage test is completed. If no message is displayed in the NIBP parameter area, it indicates that the system has no leakage. If the message "NIBP Pneumatic Leak" is displayed, it indicates that the system may have a leakage. In this case, check that all connections are in good condition and the cuff and air tubing have no leakage. Then perform the test again

NIBP overpressure: 1. Select Main Menu → Maintenance → enter the required password → Factory Maintenance → NIBP.
2. Set Patient Category to Adult/Ped in the Overpressure Protection Circuit Test. Raise the pump pressure to 320-330 mmHg. After the pressure value is stabilized, select the Test button to start a calibration, and the NIBP menu will display Test successful, if pressure is not between 320-330 mmHg, the test will fail.
3. Set Patient Category to Neo in the Overpressure Protection Circuit Test, and raise the pressure to 160-165 mmHg. After the pressure value is stabilized, select Test to start a calibration. and the NIBP menu will display Test successful, if pressure is not between 160-165 mmHg, the test will fail.

items: A Pleth wave and PR value are displayed.
NIBP: the accuracy difference between the monitor and the simulator is within ±3 mmHg.
NIBP: there is no leakage, or the manual leakage test result does not exceed 6 mmHg/min.
NIBP overpressure: test passes for Adult and Peds.
NIBP overpressure: test passes for Neo.

steps.title: CO2
steps.instructions:
Sidestream CO2 module.
1. Block the gas inlet of the module or watertrap and check for the CO2 Filterline Err alarm.
2. Enter the displayed CO2 value (6.0±0.3%).

items: Leak test: with the gas inlet blocked, the sidestream CO2 flowrate is slower than 10 ml/min and a CO2 Filterline Err alarm is given (no leakage).

steps.title: Network, battery and production test
steps.instructions: Run the production test under factory maintenance.

items: Network: the monitor can print over the network.
Network: the network printer correctly prints ECG reports.
Battery: the monitor operates correctly from battery power when external AC power fails.
Battery: the operating time of the battery meets the product specification.
Production test: all tests pass.

steps.title: Modules: BIS, NMT and BeneLink
steps.instructions:
Mark items N/A for modules that aren’t fitted.

BIS: Method:
1. Insert the BIS module to the monitor, connect the BIS cable to the Covidien simulator.
2. Connect test cable from signal generator to Covidien simulator, adjust the signal generator to output a 90Hz, 35.4mV(RMS) sine signal to the Covidien simulator. (Note: set the output mode of signal generator to HighZ module, if set to 50ohm the output will be wrong)
3. Verify the BIS waveform appears on monitor.
4. Turn on Tabular Trends review in [Main Menu] - [Review] - [Tabular Trends]. In ''Trend Group'' select BIS parameter. Set ''Interval''
(resolution) to shortest (5 seconds). Then verify EMG value ranges from 65 to 75, and SQI value should be 100. (wait a few seconds to make the SQI reading stable)
5. Turn on [BIS Setup], select [Sensor Check], verify all displayed electrodes are green (pass status).
6. If you test BISx4 module, there will be EMG L (left) and EMG R (right) values, verify both values are between 65-75. There won't be any SQI values if you test BISx4. So you only check EMG values for BISx4.

NMT: Method 1: Tools required: resistance box, multimeter.
1. Set the resistance value to 1kOhm. Connect the stimulation electrodes to the two wiring terminals.
2. Set the multimeter to operate in DC mode. Connect the multimeter sensors to the NMT stimulation electrodes, making sure that the sensor and electrode connected have the same polarity.
3. Insert the NMT module into the module rack of the monitor. Select the NMT parameter area of the monitor to access the NMT Setup menu. Set the Stimulation Current to Supra(60mA). Set the Pulse Width to 300µs. Perform a PTC measurement.
4. Check the voltage change detected by the multimeter and verify normal output of NMT stimulation.
Sensor Check
Tools required: None.
1. Connect the patient monitor, NMT module, and NMT accessories.
2. Select Main Menu → Maintenance → enter the required password → Module → NMT.
3. Follow the on-screen instructions to check the NMT sensor. If sensor check completes successfully, the message Test passed. The function of NMT sensor is OK is displayed, indicating a functional sensor. If the check fails, check whether the sensor is placed correctly as instructed, and perform the sensor check again.

BeneLink: 1. Connect the BeneLink module to the ventilator or the anesthesia machine.
2. Connect the gas supply and test lungs to the ventilator or anesthesia machine, turn on the device, and configure as follows: Setup the serial port of the external device. Setup the pressure control mode and check if the ventilator or anesthesia machine works normally.
3. Check the ID adapter is correctly configured, and the green indicator of corresponding port on the BeneLink module illuminates constantly.
4. Access [Devices Integrated] screen on the patient monitor. Check that the device type (ventilator or anesthesia machine) and ventilation mode are correctly displayed.
5. Select parameters PEEP, Pmean, VTe, MV, I:E, and f(RR) respectively on the patient monitor and check if the parameter values displayed on the patient monitor are consistent with those displayed on the ventilator or anesthesia machine.
6. Re-configure the above parameters on the ventilator or the anesthesia machine and check if the parameter values displayed on the patient monitor change accordingly.
7. Trigger alarms [MV Too Low], [Airway Pressure Too High], [PAW Too High], [Peak Too High], and [No Gas Supply] (no Air or O2) on the ventilator or the anesthesia machine. Check that these alarm messages are correctly recorded in the alarm list of the patient monitor.
8. Switch the ventilator or anesthesia machine to volume control ventilation mode. Check if the ventilation mode displayed on the patient monitor changes accordingly, and if the parameter values of PEEP, Pmean, VTe, MV, I:E, and f(RR) are correctly displayed.
Codes:
A9/Wato EX- 65 Pro - 4D52B2AE
SV 600/800 - 4D56B2AA

items: BIS: the BIS waveform appears on the monitor.
BIS: EMG value ranges from 65 to 75, and SQI value is 100 (BISx2 module).
BIS: EMG value ranges from 65 to 75 (BISx4 module).
BIS: all displayed electrodes are green during the Sensor Check test.
NMT: the voltage change is detected (33–37 V) and NMT stimulation output is normal.
NMT: the NMT passes sensor check.
BeneLink: the ID adapter is correctly configured and the green indicator of the port illuminates constantly.
BeneLink: parameter values on the monitor are consistent with the ventilator or anaesthesia machine.
BeneLink: alarm messages are correctly recorded in the monitor’s alarm list.
